This is the data centre capital of the world. They’re starting to regret it

Business is booming in Virginia’s “data centre alley”, which is generating over a billion dollars’ tax revenue – but locals say enough is enough.
By Michael Koziol
September 20, 2026

Loudoun County, Virginia: When plans first dropped for a big new data centre next to Lindsay Shaw’s home in Sterling, Virginia, she welcomed it. “It is what it is,” she thought at the time. “We’re in the data centre capital of the world.”
What she didn’t know then was that this facility by Vantage Data Centres would not be connected to the electricity grid, and would be powered by its own gas turb
Lindsay Shaw and partner Bob Salehi outside the Ashburn II Data Centre Campus, which is just metres from their home.Leigh Vogel for Sydney Morning Herald / The Age

images.alt: Lindsay Shaw and partner Bob Salehi outside the Ashburn II Data Centre Campus, which is just metres from their home.

regions.text:
“It gets so loud some nights you can hear it over the TV in my house,” says Shaw, 38. “You can hear it over the air-conditioners, you can hear it over the lawnmower, you can hear it over anything else.”
There are about 250 data centres operating or under construction in Loudoun County – the highest concentration anywhere in the world. Most were built between 2019 and 2024, but the spree has contin
The Ashburn II Data Centre Campus looms over houses in Sterling, Virginia.Sydney Morning Herald

images.alt: The Ashburn II Data Centre Campus looms over houses in Sterling, Virginia.

regions.text:
But many of the county’s 450,000 residents – like Americans around the country – have had enough. On Tuesday night, dozens spoke at a public meeting to call for a pause on data centre approvals, which the board of county supervisors ultimately voted to support.
A Loudoun resident for 20 years, Sarah Chen said: “I’ve watched it go from green pastures with livestock to feeling like livestock as our
An Amazon data centre, part of data centre alley, in Ashburn, Virginia.Bloomberg

images.alt: An Amazon data centre, part of data centre alley, in Ashburn, Virginia.

regions.text:
Loudoun County alone has more data centres than Australia. That may change if state and federal governments forge ahead with plans to encourage AI development, while imposing rules and standards on where large AI data centres can be built and the power and water they consume.
Whether Loudoun serves as a road map or a cautionary tale depends on who you talk to.
This area of Virginia, just outside W

Virginia’s state government maintains several financial incentives for data centres, reducing upfront costs and corporate income tax. County supervisor Juli Briskman says the true catalyst for the boom was the Great Recession of 2008-09, which arose from the US subprime mortgage crisis.

“Communities were struggling with their tax base and tax revenue because of the dip in housing values,” she says. “The great folks at our economic development department realised, ‘Hey, we have this fibre in the ground, we have the infrastructure in place that we could start welcoming this newish industry’. ”
Economically, there is no doubt this has been a winner for Loudoun County – which is freq
Juli Briskman, who is on the Loudoun County Board of Supervisors, says the revenue is “wonderful” but residents have had enough.Michael Koziol

images.alt: Juli Briskman, who is on the Loudoun County Board of Supervisors, says the revenue is “wonderful” but residents have had

regions.text:
That income subsidises increased services while enabling the county to reduce property taxes. It has cut real property taxes every year for the past 10 years, from $1.145 per $100 of assessed value to $0.805, saving homeowners thousands of dollars a year.
“We’ve been able to almost eliminate the car tax, which is a hated tax in Virginia,” Briskman says. “We’ve been fully funding our excellent publ

She enumerates other benefits: a mental health facility built in two years, a $US22 million cheque to acquire and preserve Oak Hill, the historic estate of former president James Monroe. “There aren’t a lot of jurisdictions in the state where they could do that.”
And yet Briskman, a Democrat, is leading the charge to crack down on data centres. “The revenue is wonderful, in large part,” she says.
Homes behind the Vantage Data Centre facility in Sterling, Virginia, which has the world’s highest concentration of data centres.

images.alt: Homes behind the Vantage Data Centre facility in Sterling, Virginia, which has the world’s highest concentration of data

regions.text:
There is a wall of back-up diesel generators, which Lindsay Shaw says were supposed to be for emergencies but end up being used once or twice a month. “When you walk out you can taste the smoke, like walking into a pack of cigarettes,” she says.
Shaw says neighbours’ children have developed respiratory illnesses that they attribute to the generators, and others have dry eye disease. “It’s been ext

Last month, its vice president of public policy, Misty Allen, told a public meeting that the company had made several improvements to reduce noise, including wrapping sound blankets around the exterior, replacing vents with noise-suppressing hoods and attaching a demister and silencer on the exhaust fans.

But the meeting was rattled when Allen revealed the facility is not expected to be connected to the power grid – and taken off the turbines – until 2040.
“It is very much our intention and desire to connect to the Dominion grid as quickly as we possibly can when capacity becomes available,” she said.
Briskman said the 2040 estimate created a problem for residents considering moving away from the a

Loudoun County had already removed the right for data centres to be built on land zoned for office use without explicit planning approval – a move matched by several Virginia counties. At Tuesday night’s meeting, the board of supervisors agreed to draft a resolution to pause new data centre applications for 12 months. It will go to a final vote next month.
Only one supervisor, Kristen Umstattd, opposed the pause.

“I worry a little bit – maybe I worry a lot – about where we’re going as a board when we seem happy to ignore one area, one industry, that provides good-paying jobs,” said Umstattd, a Democrat who has been in local politics for four decades.
“If we keep saying no – and we’ve begun to say no to these – and we shut down this industry, we’re going to lose the jobs that keep a thousand Loudoun familie
Local people complain of constant noise from nearby data centres.Sydney Morning Herald

images.alt: Local people complain of constant noise from nearby data centres.

At a local level, the backlash against data centres – and anxiety about AI more broadly – is largely bipartisan. In Congress, too, many Republicans are joining Democrats in demanding AI regulations and a slowdown.
A University of Massachusetts Amherst poll released last week found just 11 per cent of Americans – one in nine – said they would support the construction of a data centre in their local

‘I’m tired of being gaslit by being told it’s NIMBY … We choose to live here, and we deserve a beautiful county where we don’t have to fear future development’.
Sophia Chen, Loudoun County resident

President Donald Trump is trying to change that. As the sector’s own leaders sound the alarm on unchecked AI development, he leapt to defend the industry and the data centres that enable it.
